name: Jean-Marie Lehn
institution: Université de Strasbourg / Collège de France
industryTies: Institut de Science et d'Ingénierie Supramoléculaires
description: Jean-Marie Lehn coined the term 'supramolecular chemistry' and shared the 1987 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing cryptand host molecules capable of selectively binding metal cations, establishing a new chemical discipline focused on non-covalent interactions between molecules. His subsequent work on self-organizing chemical systems introduced constitutional dynamic chemistry — the concept that molecular networks can adapt and evolve toward thermodynamically optimal structures in response to external stimuli — anticipating modern materials that can self-heal and self-sort. Lehn's Strasbourg laboratory is one of the most internationally collaborative in chemistry, having trained hundreds of doctoral and postdoctoral researchers who now lead major groups on every continent. His current research program explores adaptive material networks as potential models for protocellular chemistry and the origin of life. He has received honorary doctorates from more than 30 universities and remains scientifically active in his eighties.
